title: Investigate and fix RBAC v2 SSO role-mapping race -> permission-denied / over-permissioned audit gaps
creator: Sarah Kim
description:
Summary: After RBAC v2 and SSO/SAML group-to-role mapping shipped to a subset of customers, we have two customer escalations that appear to be caused by the same root race condition: (A) users intermittently receive 'permission denied' for actions their mapped role should allow; (B) other customers see a rare over-permission where a transient mapping grants extra admin capabilities. Both cases also show incomplete audit trail entries (missing principal or mapping context) which prevents post-incident forensic analysis.

Background: RBAC v2 introduced a role cache keyed by user_id with an async refresh triggered on login / assertion. SSO/SAML group mappings update the role cache via a listener that applies deltas. We discovered that simultaneous assertion processing + a concurrent mapping-change can result in the request being evaluated against a stale or partially-applied role set. Additionally, our audit pipeline anonymizes some PII for Private deployments; the anonymization step runs before mapping context is attached, causing blank principal/mapping fields in a subset of logs.

Impact: Two paying customers escalated (one fintech tenant, one healthcare tenant) due to either blocked workflows or unintended data access. Customer impact severity: high for the fintech tenant (blocked production flows), medium for healthcare (investigation/mitigation required). We must address correctness and restore trust in audit completeness.

Repro steps (intermittent):
1) Configure SAML group 'eng-admins' -> role 'org:admin' with mapping updates enabled.
2) Simulate concurrent: A) SAML assertion login for user U; B) Mapping delta event that adds/removes group membership for U at the same time (use test harness to send both within ~50ms).
3) Observe token evaluation: sometimes the request handler reads role cache before listener completes -> permission denied. Other times the listener applies an overlapping merge that produces an extra wildcard grant -> over-permission.
4) Check audit log for the request: in affected cases principal_id or mapping_snapshot fields are empty.

Proposed fix (primary):
- Make mapping update and role cache refresh atomic per-principal. Implement per-user update locks (optimistic CAS with versioned role documents) in the role-store so assertion processing either sees pre-change or post-change consistent state, not a mix.
- Attach mapping_snapshot (group->role hash) to the auth evaluation context before any anonymization step; ensure anonymizer preserves mapping_snapshot separately.
- Add a short-lived in-memory dedupe window for mapping deltas to avoid thrash when many events arrive near-simultaneously.

Audit and recovery plan: 
- Add a migration job that recomputes role-cache for affected orgs (api endpoint /admin/roles/recompute) and mark completed on tenant.
- Backfill missing audit entries where possible by reprocessing raw auth traces and adding mapping_snapshot (best-effort). Log backfill results and notify customers.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for optimistic CAS and versioned role docs.
- Integration tests that simulate concurrent SAML assertion + mapping delta at varying latencies (0ms, 10ms, 50ms, 200ms).
- End-to-end test against Private deployment image to verify anonymization order doesn't drop mapping_snapshot.
- Chaos test on staging with scaled concurrent mapping changes.

Rollout plan:
1) Patch runtime (role-store + listener) in canary cluster; run regression + chaos tests.
2) Deploy to hosted - opt-in customers first (notify CS).
3) Coordinate with Private/Dedicated release owners for patch versions.
4) After 48h monitoring, progressively release to remaining customers.

Observability:
- Add a new metric rbac.mapping_concurrent_conflicts and a trace tag rbac.mapping_version_on_eval.
- Create dashboard card showing rate of auth_evals with empty mapping_snapshot.

PRs and artifacts: 
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8342 - "role-store: versioned role docs + CAS apply"
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8361 - "saml-listener: attach mapping_snapshot before anonymizer"
- Integration test harness: github.com/redwood-inference/tests/pull/211
- Incident notes (customer-facing): drive.redwood.ai/esc-2025-11-rbac-sso-01 (private, CS owns distribution)

Acceptance criteria: 
- Auth regression tests pass (no flakes in simulated concurrent scenarios).
- No new customer reports for 7 days post-rollout.
- Audit logs consistently contain mapping_snapshot for >99.9% of auth events in canary.

Follow-ups: 
- Evaluate replacing per-user locks with a lock-free merge algorithm in Q1 2026 (research spike).
- Add documentation on SAML mapping eventual consistency guarantees for Support and Customer Success teams.

Notes: This ticket is P0 due to active customer escalations. Coordinate with CS (Emma Torres) and legal for tenants in regulated industries.
